6B.01.t: Anterior Approach to the Hip — Smith-Petersen & DAA
6B.01.b:
### Step by step
[[FIG: Fig 6B.2, 6B.3, 6B.4 · 6B.01
- Position → supine · Incision → front half of the iliac crest → ASIS (anterior superior iliac spine) → 8–10 cm down toward the lateral patella
- Superficial plane → **sartorius (femoral) / TFL (tensor fasciae latae; superior gluteal)** · deep plane → **rectus femoris (femoral) / gluteus medius (superior gluteal)**

1) Find the gap **5–8 cm below the ASIS**; open the fascia **over the TFL** belly
2) Ligate the ascending LFCA (lateral femoral circumflex artery) → rectus heads off → T capsulotomy

### Dangers
[[FIG: Fig 6B.5, 6B.6 · 6B.01
- At risk → **LFCN** crosses sartorius ≈2.5 cm below the ASIS · **ascending LFCA** · femoral nerve medial to rectus · head blood supply (superolateral neck)

### DAA — the anterior THA version
- DAA (direct anterior approach) → distal half of Smith-Petersen, same plane
- **Iliocapsularis** retractor → anterior wall, femoral nerve shielded · femur → superior + inferior capsule only, **never the posterior structures**

PITFALL — the deep plane of the DAA
- Hopp → rectus femoris / **gluteus medius** · Sherif Khaled → rectus femoris / **TFL**
- Say → "**superficial sartorius / TFL, deep rectus / gluteus medius** — all femoral vs superior gluteal"

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "anterior approach to the hip"
- Plane → sartorius + rectus (**femoral**) / TFL + medius (**superior gluteal**) → true internervous
- Open the fascia over TFL → LFCN safe medially
- Ligate the **ascending LFCA** in the gap
- Rectus heads off → T capsulotomy
- Danger list → LFCN, ascending LFCA, femoral nerve, head blood supply

### Step by step

- Say → "**intermuscular, not internervous** → TFL and medius share the superior gluteal nerve"

6B.04.t: Posterior Approach to the Hip — Moore / Southern
6B.04.b:
### Step by step
[[FIG: Fig 6B.17, 6B.18, 6B.19, 6B.20, 6B.21 · 6B.04
- Position → true lateral · Incision → 6–8 cm above-behind the greater trochanter, in the line of maximus → down the shaft 10–13 cm
- Interval → none → **split gluteus maximus** (supply enters far medially)

1) Split maximus ≤7 cm above the greater trochanter
2) **Palpate** the sciatic nerve; never dissect it

### Dangers
- At risk → **sciatic nerve** (peroneal division; knee flexed, hip extended for closure) · inferior gluteal artery under piriformis → retracts into the pelvis · **MFCA** under quadratus femoris (keep quadratus + obturator externus)

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "posterior approach to the hip"
- No internervous plane → split maximus in its fibres
- Flex + IR → piriformis, gemelli + obturator internus cut near the greater trochanter, reflected over the **sciatic nerve**
- Keep **quadratus femoris + obturator externus** → MFCA
- T capsulotomy → dislocate in flexion + IR
- Close → capsule + rotators repaired → lower dislocation
